metrics.summary: The importer in ledger/importer.py hand-rolled CSV parsing with `line.split(",")`, which broke on quoted fields containing commas and escaped quotes (so "ACME, Inc." split into two cells), and `_parse_amount` didn't strip thousands separators (so "-1,250.00" raised "could not convert string to float"). Fix: `parse_rows` now uses the stdlib `csv` module over `io.StringIO(text)` (which correctly handles quoted commas, `""` escapes and newlines inside quoted fields), keeping the original semantics — rows with no non-whitespace cells (blank lines) are skipped, and header is still lowercased/stripped with the same missing-column error. `_parse_amount` now also strips commas, so quoted amounts like "-1,250.00" parse correctly. Verified with the user's exact file via `python -m ledger.cli import march.csv` (3 transactions, net -1296.70), plus ad-hoc checks for escaped quotes and embedded line breaks. All 5 pre-existing tests still pass, and I added 3 regression tests in tests/test_importer.py (quoted comma + escaped quotes, thousands-separator amount, line break in quoted field) — 8/8 pass.
